land.text: Mayyafariqin and the Diyarbakir area, taken by Badh ibn Dustak after the death of the Buyid emir Adud al-Dawla in 983

predecessors.note: The Hamdanids of Mosul and Aleppo also held fortresses in the region (retaken 991-997).

land.text: Diyar Bakr: Mayyafariqin, Amid, Akhlat, Manzikert, Nisibis, Ercis, Muradiye, Siirt, Cizre and Hasankeyf; "Henceforth, the Diyar Bakr fell almost entirely under the direct rule of the Seljuks"

capitals.name: Mayyafariqin (Silvan)
capitals.note: The page says the realm was "centered on the city of Mayyafariqin" in one place and "centered on the city of Amid" (Diyarbakir) in another; no years for a move are given.

rulers.name: Badh ibn Dustak

rulers.name: Abu Ali al-Hasan ibn Marwan
rulers.note: killed at Amid in 997 by rebellious inhabitants

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Marwanid row): after Adud al-Dawla died in 983 "Badh took Mayyafariqin and conquered Diyarbakir". The Badh page says he had Mayyafariqin and the whole Diyarbakir area by 984. No page gives an area.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Badh "also took towns on the northern shore of Lake Van" (the Badh page: Malazgirt 978/979; Ercis, Ahlat and Bargiri later; no year). The 984 start is bridging.

correction.text: Diyarbakir, Lake Van and Hisn Kayfa (Hasankeyf)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: after Badh's death al-Hasan "returned to Hisn Kayfa and retook fortresses from the Hamdanids" (991-997).

correction.text: Diyar Bakr: Mayyafariqin, Amid, Akhlat, Manzikert, Nisibis, Ercis, Muradiye, Siirt, Cizre, Hasankayf

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Nasr al-Dawla "subdued his vassal Ibn Dimne in Diyarbakir in 1011"; the territory list (Mayyafariqin, Amid, Akhlat, Manzikert, Nisibis, Ercis, Muradiye, Siirt, Cizre, Hasankayf) is undated, so Siirt, Cizre and Nisibis are drawn from here as bridging.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: "He took Edessa in 1026, but Byzantine forces under George Maniakes retook it in 1031."
New keyframe: Edessa lost to the Byzantines in 1031.

correction.text: Diyar Bakr with Edessa recaptured by Bal

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: "His commander Bal recaptured it in 1032, and the Byzantines took it again in 1033."

correction.text: Diyar Bakr under Seljuk overlordship from 1054

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1033-1085: Diyar Bakr; "Nasr al-Dawla acknowledged Toghrul Beg as overlord in 1054 but kept his territories"; Jazirat ibn Umar (Cizre) was the last emir's remaining city. The Nasr page dates the last Edessa recapture to 1035 instead.

ledger.note: 983: Badh ibn Dustak, a Kurdish shepherd, seizes Mayyafariqin. 'After Buyid emir Adud al-Dawla died in 983, Badh took Mayyafariqin and conquered Diyarbakir' (infobox 983/990-1085). The Badh page: 'In 984, he had captured' Mayyafaraqin and the whole Diyarbakir area.

region.text: the northern shore of Lake Van: Malazgirt, Ercis, Ahlat

ledger.counterpart: local Armenian and Arab lords of the Lake Van shore
ledger.note: 984: towns on the north shore of Lake Van. 'He also took towns on the northern shore of Lake Van'; the Badh page has him capturing Malazgirt in 978/979 and Ercis, Ahlat and Bargiri 'later'. The year is bridging, from the Badh page's 984 for Mayyafariqin.

region.text: Hisn Kayfa and the fortresses retaken from the Hamdanids

ledger.note: 991: al-Hasan retakes fortresses from the Hamdanids. 'After Badh's death, his nephew al-Hasan returned to Hisn Kayfa and retook fortresses from the Hamdanids' (991-997).

region.text: Diyarbakir (Amid), ruled by the vassal Ibn Dimne

ledger.note: 1011: Nasr al-Dawla takes over Diyarbakir directly. 'He subdued his vassal Ibn Dimne in Diyarbakir in 1011.' The town had been the scene of al-Hasan's murder by rebellious inhabitants in 997.

1026: Nasr al-Dawla takes Edessa. 'He took Edessa in 1026, but Byzantine forces under George Maniakes retook it in 1031.' [Reviewer me-08-x, 2026-10-19: counterpart was byzantine-empire; the Numayrid page: 'the Numayrids also controlled Edessa until the Byzantines conquered it in the early 1030s', and has Nasr al-Dawla kill the Numayrid Utayr and capture the city (dated 1030 there).]
1031: the Byzantines under George Maniakes retake Edessa.
1032: Nasr al-Dawla's commander Bal recaptures Edessa.
1033: 'the Byzantines took it again in 1033.' (The Nasr al-Dawla page has Edessa seized in 1026 and recaptured in 1035.)

region.text: Diyar Bakr: Diyarbakir, Mayyafariqin, Ahlat, Cizre, Bitlis, Siirt and Hasankeyf

ledger.note: 1085: the Seljuks end the Marwanid dynasty. 'The end of the Marwanid dynasty came about by treason': the former vizier Ibn Jahir persuaded Malik-Shah I and Nizam al-Mulk to attack Mayyafariqin; 'Henceforth, the Diyar Bakr fell almost entirely under the direct rule of the Seljuks.' The Malik-Shah page names Diyarbakir, Mayyafariqin, Ahlat, Cizre, Bitlis, Siirt, Erzen and Hasankeyf as taken.
1085: the last emir Nasir al-Dawla Mansur falls; Jazirat ibn Umar (Cizre) was his remaining city. The page gives no month and dates no Malik-Shah campaign to 1085 except as the end of the dynasty.

wars.name: Badh ibn Dustak against the Buyids and Hamdanids
wars.outcome: Badh took Mayyafariqin and Diyarbakir in 983-984; his brother Abu l-Fawaris Hasan was killed fighting the Buyids in 987-988 and Badh himself was killed in battle against the Hamdanids in 991.
wars.note: The Marwanid page says he conquered Diyarbakir after 983; the Badh page says Mayyafariqin and the Diyarbakir area were his by 984. The Marwanid page has him taking the plain of Mush in Taron during Bardas Phokas's rebellion; the Badh page has him raiding Taron and sacking Mush for Bardas Skleros: no border move written.

wars.name: Marwanid-Byzantine struggle for Edessa
wars.outcome: Nasr al-Dawla took Edessa in 1026; Maniakes retook it in 1031, Bal recaptured it in 1032 and the Byzantines took it again in 1033.
wars.note: The Nasr al-Dawla page gives seized 1026 and recaptured 1035.

wars.name: Seljuk conquest of Diyar Bakr
wars.outcome: Malik-Shah I, urged by the traitor Ibn Jahir, took Mayyafariqin and Diyar Bakr; the Marwanid dynasty ended with Nasir al-Dawla Mansur in 1085.

certainty.note: A hill country of fortress towns; no treaty lines on the pages. Edessa and the Lake Van shore are the least certain.

notes: Cliopatria has no Marwanid row. Wikidata id not known; left null. No page opened gives an area. Disagreements: Badh's start 983 (Marwanid page, after Adud al-Dawla's death) vs 984 (Badh page) vs 990 (infobox); Badh's death at Mosul (infobox) vs killed in battle against the Hamdanids (text); Edessa recaptured 1033 (Marwanid page) vs 1035 (Nasr page). Not written as events: the Mush/Taron operations (987-989), Bardas Skleros and Phokas rebellions, Said's 1000 submission to Basil II as magistros and doux of the East (a Byzantine tributary relation: byzantine-empire should carry a vassal_start with this state as counterpart), Nasr al-Dawla's acknowledgement of Toghrul Beg in 1054 (Seljuk vassal_start belongs in the Seljuk dossiers; the page says he 'kept his territories'), the temporary rule of Mosul and Edessa the page mentions without years, the Uqaylid border (the Marwanid page does not mention the Uqaylids; the Malik-Shah page has Muslim ibn Quraysh and the Marwanid Mansur fleeing together to Diyarbakir). Nusaybin ('Nisibis'), Siirt and Cizre are drawn from 1011 as bridging because the territory list is undated. Gazetteer names needed: Mayyafariqin (Silvan), Akhlat (Ahlat), Cizre, Hasankeyf, Ercis (drawn here as a coordinate), Jazirat ibn Umar.
